title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: an abstract 'Remarque' inside the axiomatisation (axioms C1–C8 on the preceding pages) of a geometric situation in the 1986 'Analysis situs' draft. 𝓕 is a set of geometric objects, perhaps closed parts, strata or 'faces'; this is unsure. It carries two partial orders, ≤ and ≼, presumably inclusion-like and specialisation/face-like.

In the diagrams the vertical symbol under an object means 'is ≥/≽ the object below'.

The axioms abstracted here:
(a) Given G ≼ F and F' ≤ F, there is a unique G' with G' ≤ G and G' ≼ F'. This is a unique-lifting or 'restriction' property: a ≤-smaller F' of F induces a unique ≼-partner G' inside G. It amounts to saying that ≼, seen as a relation, is a discrete-fibration-like correspondence along ≤.
(b) Given G ≤ F and a vertical G' below G, one can complete (not necessarily uniquely) to G' ≤ F' with F' below F. For this to be non-trivial, the verticals in (b) must be ≼ (otherwise F' = F works by transitivity). So (b) says: G' ≼ G ≤ F implies there is F' with G' ≤ F' ≼ F. In relational terms, ≼∘≤ ⊆ ≤∘≼, a commutation or 'distributive-law' condition.
(c) A mixed antisymmetry: F ≤ G ≼ F implies F = G. The parenthetical 'G ≼ F ≤ G' is the same cycle read from G.

Claim (i): define G ≪ F iff there exists F' with G ≤ F' ≼ F, i.e. ≪ is the composite relation ≤∘≼. Then ≪ is a partial order.
- Reflexivity is clear.
- Transitivity: from H ≤ G' ≼ G ≤ F' ≼ F, apply (b) to G' ≼ G ≤ F'. This gives F'' with G' ≤ F'' ≼ F', hence H ≤ F'' ≼ F.
- Antisymmetry: start from G ≤ F' ≼ F ≤ G' ≼ G.
  - (b) applied to F' ≼ F ≤ G' gives X with F' ≤ X ≼ G'. Then G ≤ X ≼ G' ≼ G, so (c) gives X = G, and then G ≼ G' ≼ G gives G' = G.
  - Then F ≤ G ≤ F' ≼ F, so (c) gives F' = F, and G ≤ F ≤ G gives F = G.

This is the abstract version of the concrete argument on p.83 (via C7, C8). The next page (85) states that the (a)-squares are cartesian (G' = Inf_≪(F', G)), and that ≤-cartesian squares are ≪-cartesian. It then laments that one should isolate minimal axioms giving the 'evident formal properties' of the geometric notions.

Purpose: to extract a minimal formal calculus of two interacting orders underlying the analysis-situs constructions.
errors: The note says the order property of ≪ 'ne suppose que a) b)'. The proof actually uses only (b) (for transitivity) and (b)+(c) (for antisymmetry); (a) is not needed. Probably a slip for 'b) c)', unless the reading is wrong.
As transcribed, (b) has ≤ in both vertical positions, which makes it trivial (take F' = F). The verticals must be ≼ for (b) to be meaningful and for the transitivity proof to work.

ideas.what: Composite of two partial orders ≤∘≼ is again a preorder when ≼∘≤ ⊆ ≤∘≼ (commutation/'distributive law' condition b), and is antisymmetric under the mixed antisymmetry c)
ideas.modern_name: Composition of preorders / distributive law between relations (relation algebra); factorisation-system-like decomposition of an order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in relation algebra and category theory (distributive laws: Beck 1969, for monads; for posets this is elementary)

ideas.what: Unique completion of squares (axiom a): G ≼ F and F' ≤ F give a unique G' ≤ G with G' ≼ F', later shown to be the ≪-infimum (cartesian square)
ideas.modern_name: Unique lifting / discrete-fibration-like property; cartesian squares in a poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Grothendieck fibrations, SGA1; elementary for posets)
ideas.where_published: The general notion of cartesian square/fibration is in SGA1 VI; this specific poset axiom does not appear there

missed.claim: This page is part of an attempt, apparently never completed or published, to give a minimal axiomatics ('axiomes C1–C8') for the formal order-theoretic properties of geometric objects in the 1986 Analysis situs draft. The page itself contains only an elementary lemma.
missed.quote: Posant G ≪ F ⟺def ∃ F' avec G ≤ F' ≼ F, la relation ≪ est une relation d'ordre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's 1986 programme of axiomatising 'analysis situs' (tame-topology-like) combinatorics. The lemma itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary order-theoretic lemma (composite of two commuting partial orders is a partial order). Historically interesting only as a fragment of the unpublished analysis-situs axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: In (b), the vertical relations are presumably ≼ (G' ≼ G, F' ≼ F) rather than ≤; the handwritten vertical symbols are ambiguous, and with ≤ the axiom is vacuous.
In (c), the alternative form reads 'G ≼ F ≤ G' (the same cycle F ≤ G ≼ F read from G), not 'G ≽ F ≤ G'.
The final line 'ne suppose que a) b)' is mathematically 'b) c)'; this is a possible misreading, or Grothendieck's slip.
